sentences.cn_text: 英国的铁路运营商如何能为再次上调铁路客运票价找到合理依据？
sentences.en_text: How can Britain’s train operators possibly justify yet another increase to rail passenger fares?

sentences.cn_text: 这已成为一项令人沮丧却又极为可靠的年度惯例：每年一月，火车票价都会上涨，给那些别无选择只能依靠铁路网络上班或出行的人群增添了沉重的额外负担。
sentences.en_text: It has become a grimly reliable annual ritual: every January the cost of travelling by train rises, imposing a significant extra burden on those who have no option but to use the rail network to get to work or otherwise.

sentences.cn_text: 今年平均2.7%的涨幅虽略低于去年，但仍远高于官方消费者价格指数（CPI）所衡量的通胀水平。
sentences.en_text: This year’s rise, an average of 2.7 percent, may be a fraction lower than last year’s, but it is still well above the official Consumer Price Index (CPI) measure of inflation.

sentences.cn_text: 历届政府允许此类涨价的理由是，铁路网络的投资和运营成本应由使用者承担，而非全体纳税人负担。
sentences.en_text: Successive governments have permitted such increases on the grounds that the cost of investing in and running the rail network should be borne by those who use it, rather than the general taxpayer.

sentences.cn_text: 按照这种论调，为什么一位来自林肯郡的开车退休老人要为一位来自萨里郡的股票经纪人的日常通勤买单？
sentences.en_text: Why, the argument goes, should a car-driving pensioner from Lincolnshire have to subsidise the daily commute of a stockbroker from Surrey?

sentences.cn_text: 同样，人们也认为，东南部通勤者的困境——其中许多人将面临最大幅度的涨价——相比那些必须忍受中部和北部地区相对落后基础设施的人，得到了过多的关注。
sentences.en_text: Equally, there is a sense that the travails of commuters in the South East, many of whom will face among the biggest rises, have received too much attention compared to those who must endure the relatively poor infrastructure of the Midlands and the North.

sentences.cn_text: 然而，在过去12个月中，这些通勤者也经历了多年来最为严重的铁路罢工。
sentences.en_text: However, over the past 12 months, those commuters have also experienced some of the worst rail strikes in years.

sentences.cn_text: 铁路运营商大肆宣扬其对铁路网络的改进固然不错，但乘客理应期待获得基本水平的服务，因为他们如今为出行支付了可观的费用。
sentences.en_text: It is all very well train operators trumpeting the improvements they are making to the network, but passengers should be able to expect a basic level of service for the substantial sums they are now paying to travel.

sentences.cn_text: 最近这波罢工的责任在于工会。
sentences.en_text: The responsibility for the latest wave of strikes rests on the unions.

sentences.cn_text: 然而，有充分理由表明，那些受罢工影响最严重的人应就其所遭受的干扰获得补偿。
sentences.en_text: However, there is a strong case that those who have been worst affected by industrial action should receive compensation for the disruption they have suffered.

sentences.cn_text: 政府已承诺修改法律以引入最低服务要求，以便即便发生罢工，服务也能继续运转。
sentences.en_text: The Government has pledged to change the law to introduce a minimum service requirement so that, even when strikes occur, services can continue to operate.

sentences.cn_text: 这应当成为解决英国铁路长期问题的更广泛一揽子措施的组成部分。
sentences.en_text: This should form part of a wider package of measures to address the long-running problems on Britain’s railways.

sentences.cn_text: 诚然，需要更多投资，但如果乘客还必须忍受拥挤、不可靠的服务，以及时刻表变更时的频繁混乱，或计划维护管理不善带来的问题，他们就不会无限期地愿意支付更多费用。
sentences.en_text: Yes, more investment is needed, but passengers will not be willing to pay more indefinitely if they must also endure cramped, unreliable services, interrupted by regular chaos when timetables are changed, or planned maintenance is managed incompetently.

sentences.cn_text: 国有化的威胁目前或许已被化解，但若不尽快解决乘客的合理愤怒，它将以更猛烈的方式卷土重来。
sentences.en_text: The threat of nationalisation may have been seen off for now, but it will return with a vengeance if the justified anger of passengers is not addressed in short order.
